pages.caption: There once lived a poor tailor, who had a son called Aladdin.
pages.scene: A poor tailor's shop in a city. The walls are bare, and the room is humble and sparse. A small workbench sits by the window with a few scraps of cloth.

pages.caption: A careless, idle boy who would do nothing but play ball all day long.
pages.scene: A dusty street in the city, lined with simple buildings. A group of small boys are gathered in a clear patch of ground.
pages.action: Aladdin plays ball in the streets with the other boys.

pages.caption: This so grieved the father that he died.
pages.scene: The interior of the tailor's shop, now dimmer. Mustapha sits at his workbench, his face lined with worry and exhaustion.

pages.caption: In spite of the mother's tears and prayers, Aladdin did not mend his ways.
pages.scene: A simple home. Aladdin's mother sits weeping, a handkerchief to her face. Aladdin stands nearby, unmoved.

pages.caption: A stranger asked him his age, and if he was not the son of Mustapha the tailor.
pages.scene: The same dusty street as before. Aladdin plays ball as usual. A stranger in dark robes approaches him from behind.
pages.action: The stranger asks Aladdin his age and if he is the son of Mustapha.

pages.caption: The stranger fell on his neck and kissed him, saying, I am your uncle.
pages.scene: The street. The magician, disguised as a wealthy traveller, embraces Aladdin warmly.
pages.action: The magician falls on Aladdin's neck and kisses him.

pages.caption: Aladdin ran home and told his mother of his newly found uncle.
pages.scene: The interior of Aladdin's home. Aladdin runs in breathlessly to tell his mother the news.
pages.action: Aladdin speaks excitedly to his mother.

pages.caption: Indeed, child, your father had a brother, but I always thought he was dead.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin's mother looks doubtful, her brow furrowed with uncertainty.

pages.caption: However, she prepared supper, and bade Aladdin seek his uncle, who came laden with wine and fruit.
pages.scene: The home, now set with a modest supper. Wine and fruit sit on the table. The magician enters, laden with provisions.
pages.action: The magician enters carrying wine and fruit.

pages.caption: He presently fell down and kissed the place where Mustapha used to sit.
pages.scene: The home. The magician kneels and kisses the empty chair where Mustapha used to sit.
pages.action: The magician falls down and kisses the place where Mustapha used to sit.

pages.caption: He bade Aladdin's mother not to be surprised at not having seen him before.
pages.scene: The home. The magician sits at the table, speaking to Aladdin's mother with an air of explanation.

pages.caption: He then turned to Aladdin, and asked him his trade.
pages.scene: The home. The magician turns to Aladdin, who stands sheepishly before him.
pages.action: The magician asks Aladdin his trade.

pages.caption: At which the boy hung his head, while his mother burst into tears.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin hangs his head in shame. His mother weeps.
pages.action: Aladdin hangs his head; his mother bursts into tears.

pages.caption: He offered to take a shop for him and stock it with merchandise.
pages.scene: The home. The magician stands, gesturing warmly toward Aladdin.
pages.action: The magician offers to set Aladdin up in a shop.

pages.caption: Next day he bought Aladdin a fine suit of clothes and took him all over the city.
pages.scene: The next day. A fine suit of clothes is laid out. Aladdin stands in the street wearing the new garment.
pages.action: The magician leads Aladdin through the city.

pages.caption: He brought him home at nightfall to his mother, who was overjoyed.
pages.scene: The city streets at dusk. The magician walks Aladdin home through the bustling market.
pages.action: The magician brings Aladdin home at nightfall.

pages.caption: The next day the magician led Aladdin into some beautiful gardens.
pages.scene: Beautiful gardens outside the city gates. Lush trees and flowering bushes line a winding path. A stone fountain gushes water in the centre.
pages.action: The magician leads Aladdin into the gardens.

pages.caption: They sat down by a fountain.
pages.scene: The gardens. Aladdin and the magician sit on a stone bench beside the fountain.
pages.action: They sit down by the fountain.

pages.caption: The magician pulled a cake from his girdle, which he divided between them.
pages.scene: The gardens. The magician pulls a cake from his girdle and breaks it in two.
pages.action: The magician divides the cake between them.

pages.caption: They then journeyed onward till they almost reached the mountains.
pages.scene: A rocky path ascending toward distant mountains. The ground grows rougher and the air thinner.
pages.action: They journey onward toward the mountains.

pages.caption: Aladdin was so tired that he begged to go back, but the magician beguiled him.
pages.scene: The rocky path. Aladdin walks slowly, exhausted, his shoulders slumped.
pages.action: Aladdin begs to go back, but the magician leads him on.

pages.caption: At last they came to two mountains divided by a narrow valley.
pages.scene: Two great mountains stand on either side of a narrow valley. The ground is barren and strange.

pages.caption: We will go no farther, said the false uncle.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician stands firm, gesturing for Aladdin to stop.
pages.action: The magician declares they will go no farther.

pages.caption: Only do you gather up sticks while I kindle a fire.
pages.scene: The valley. Aladdin gathers dry sticks and branches, piling them on the ground.

pages.caption: When it was lit the magician threw on it a powder, at the same time saying some magical words.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician lights the fire and throws powder upon it. He speaks strange words.
pages.action: The magician throws powder on the fire and speaks magical words.

pages.caption: The earth trembled a little and opened, disclosing a square flat stone with a brass ring.
pages.scene: The valley. The earth trembles and splits open. A square flat stone with a brass ring in the centre appears.

pages.caption: Aladdin tried to run away, but the magician caught him and gave him a blow.
pages.scene: The valley. Aladdin turns and tries to flee. The magician catches him and strikes him.
pages.action: Aladdin tries to run away; the magician catches him and gives him a blow.

pages.caption: What have I done, uncle? he said piteously.
pages.scene: The valley. Aladdin lies on the ground, dazed. The magician looms over him.

pages.caption: Fear nothing, but obey me. Beneath this stone lies a treasure.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician speaks more kindly now, gesturing toward the stone.

pages.caption: You must do exactly as I tell you.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician points down at the stone, explaining the rules.

pages.caption: At the word treasure Aladdin forgot his fears, and grasped the ring.
pages.scene: The valley. Aladdin kneels and grasps the brass ring. His face is eager now.
pages.action: Aladdin grasps the ring, saying the names of his father and grandfather.

pages.caption: The stone came up quite easily, and some steps appeared.
pages.scene: The valley. The stone lifts easily, revealing a flight of steps descending into darkness.

pages.caption: Go down, said the magician; at the foot of those steps you will find an open door.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician stands at the mouth of the cave, instructing Aladdin.

pages.caption: Tuck up your gown and go through them without touching anything, or you will die.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician continues his instructions, holding up a warning finger.

pages.caption: These halls lead into a garden of fine fruit trees.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician describes the garden beyond the halls.

pages.caption: Walk on until you come to a niche in a terrace where stands a lighted lamp.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician speaks of the lamp.

pages.caption: Pour out the oil it contains, and bring it to me.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician instructs Aladdin to pour out the oil and bring the lamp.

pages.caption: He drew a ring from his finger and gave it to Aladdin, bidding him prosper.
pages.scene: The valley. The magician draws a ring from his finger and gives it to Aladdin.
pages.action: The magician gives Aladdin a ring.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The cave mouth. Aladdin descends the steps into the darkness.

pages.caption: At the foot of those steps he found an open door leading into three large halls.
pages.scene: Three large halls stretch before Aladdin, filled with treasures and goods. The air is cool and still.
pages.action: Aladdin tucks up his gown and walks through the halls without touching anything.

pages.caption: The halls lead into a garden of fine fruit trees.
pages.scene: Beyond the halls, a lush garden of fine fruit trees stretches out, laden with sparkling fruit.

pages.caption: He came to a niche in a terrace where stood a lighted lamp.
pages.scene: A terrace in the garden. In a niche stands a lighted lamp, its flame steady and bright.
pages.action: Aladdin pours out the oil from the lamp.

pages.caption: He gathered some fruit off the trees, and having got the lamp, arrived at the mouth of the cave.
pages.scene: The garden. Aladdin gathers some fruit from the trees, which are in reality precious stones.
pages.action: Aladdin gathers fruit off the trees.

pages.caption: The magician cried out in a great hurry: Make haste and give me the lamp.
pages.scene: The cave mouth. The magician waits impatiently above, peering down into the darkness.
pages.action: The magician cries out for the lamp.

pages.caption: This Aladdin refused to do until he was out of the cave.
pages.scene: The cave mouth. Aladdin stands just inside the darkness, the lamp clutched to his chest.
pages.action: Aladdin refuses to give up the lamp until he is out of the cave.

pages.caption: The magician flew into a terrible passion, and throwing some more powder on the fire.
pages.scene: The cave mouth. The magician's face contorts with rage. He throws more powder on the fire.
pages.action: The magician flies into a passion and throws powder on the fire.

pages.caption: He said something, and the stone rolled back into its place.
pages.scene: The cave mouth. The magician speaks magical words. The great stone rolls back into place, sealing the entrance.
pages.action: The magician says something, and the stone rolls back into place.

pages.caption: The magician left Persia for ever.
pages.scene: The cave mouth. The magician walks away into the distance, leaving the sealed stone behind.

pages.caption: He was no uncle of Aladdin's, but a cunning magician, who had read in his magic books.
pages.scene: A flashback. The magician's true nature is revealed â€” he is no uncle, but a cunning magician who read of the lamp in his magic books.

pages.caption: Though he alone knew where to find it, he could only receive it from the hand of another.
pages.scene: The sealed cave. Darkness presses in from all sides. Silence.

pages.caption: He had picked out the foolish Aladdin, intending to get the lamp and kill him afterward.
pages.scene: The sealed cave. The magician's cruel plan is laid bare â€” he intended to kill Aladdin once he had the lamp.

pages.caption: For two days Aladdin remained in the dark, crying and lamenting.
pages.scene: Complete darkness inside the sealed cave. Aladdin sits alone, weeping.

pages.caption: At last he clasped his hands in prayer, and in so doing rubbed the ring.
pages.scene: The darkness. Aladdin clasps his hands together in prayer.
pages.action: Aladdin clasps his hands in prayer, rubbing the ring on his finger.

pages.caption: An enormous and frightful genie rose out of the earth, saying: What wouldst thou with me?
pages.characters: The Genie of the Ring, Aladdin
pages.scene: The darkness. A blinding light erupts from the ring. An enormous, frightful genie rises from the earth.

pages.caption: I am the Slave of the Ring, and will obey thee in all things.
pages.characters: The Genie of the Ring, Aladdin
pages.scene: The darkness. The genie towers above Aladdin, fearsome and mighty.

pages.caption: Aladdin fearlessly replied: Deliver me from this place!
pages.scene: The darkness. Aladdin stands firm despite his fear, looking up at the genie.

pages.caption: Whereupon the earth opened, and he found himself outside.
pages.scene: The earth opens beneath Aladdin. Light floods in as he is lifted upward.

pages.caption: As soon as his eyes could bear the light he went home.
pages.scene: The city street at dawn. Aladdin stands blinking in the light, disoriented and weak.
pages.action: Aladdin walks home, his eyes adjusting to the light.

pages.caption: But he fainted on the threshold.
pages.scene: The threshold of Aladdin's home. He collapses on the doorstep.

pages.caption: When he came to himself he told his mother what had passed.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin lies on a mat, his mother kneeling beside him. He recounts his adventure.
pages.action: Aladdin tells his mother what has passed.

pages.caption: He showed her the lamp and the fruits, which were in reality precious stones.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin shows his mother the lamp and the fruits he gathered.
pages.action: Aladdin displays the lamp and the precious stones.

pages.caption: He then asked for some food.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin looks hungry and weary, asking for food.

pages.caption: Alas! child, she said, I have nothing in the house.
pages.scene: The home. His mother looks around the bare room, her face filled with despair.

pages.caption: But I have spun a little cotton and will go and sell it.
pages.scene: The home. His mother gestures toward a small bundle of spun cotton.

pages.caption: Aladdin bade her keep her cotton, for he would sell the lamp instead.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin stops her, gesturing toward the lamp.
pages.action: Aladdin bids his mother keep her cotton.

pages.caption: As it was very dirty she began to rub it, that it might fetch a higher price.
pages.scene: The home. His mother picks up the dirty lamp and begins to rub it to make it presentable.

pages.caption: Instantly a hideous genie appeared, and asked what she would have.
pages.characters: The Genie of the Lamp, Aladdin's mother
pages.scene: The home. A hideous genie appears in a cloud of smoke, towering over the room.
pages.action: The genie appears and asks what she would have.

pages.caption: She fainted away.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin's mother collapses to the floor in terror.

pages.caption: Aladdin, snatching the lamp, said boldly: Fetch me something to eat!
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin seizes the lamp from his mother's hand, standing bold before the genie.
pages.action: Aladdin snatches the lamp and commands the genie.

pages.caption: The genie returned with a silver bowl, twelve silver plates containing rich meats.
pages.scene: The home. The genie returns carrying a silver bowl and twelve silver plates laden with rich meats, two silver cups, and two bottles of wine.
pages.action: The genie returns with the feast.

pages.caption: Aladdin's mother, when she came to herself, said: Whence comes this splendid feast?
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin's mother stirs and opens her eyes, seeing the magnificent feast spread before her.
pages.action: She comes to herself and sees the feast.

pages.caption: Ask not, but eat, replied Aladdin.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin gestures toward the food, smiling.

pages.caption: So they sat at breakfast till it was dinner-time.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin and his mother sit eating the feast. Hours pass.
pages.action: They sit at breakfast till it is dinner-time.

pages.caption: Aladdin told his mother about the lamp.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin tells his mother about the lamp and its powers.
pages.action: Aladdin tells his mother about the lamp.

pages.caption: She begged him to sell it, and have nothing to do with devils.
pages.scene: The home. His mother pleads with Aladdin, her face anxious.
pages.action: She begs him to sell the lamp and have nothing to do with devils.

pages.caption: No, said Aladdin, since chance hath made us aware of its virtues, we will use it.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin shakes his head firmly, the ring visible on his finger.

pages.caption: And the ring likewise, which I shall always wear on my finger.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin touches the ring on his finger.

pages.caption: When they had eaten all the genie had brought, Aladdin sold one of the silver plates.
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The home. The last silver plate sits on the table. Aladdin looks at it, then rubs the lamp.

pages.caption: He then had recourse to the genie, who gave him another set of plates.
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The home. The genie appears once more with a fresh set of silver plates.

pages.caption: Thus they lived for many years.
pages.scene: The home. Years pass. The room is now modestly furnished. Aladdin and his mother live comfortably.

pages.caption: One day Aladdin heard an order from the Sultan proclaimed.
pages.scene: The city streets. A herald walks through the marketplace, a scroll in his hand. People gather to listen.

pages.caption: Everyone was to stay at home and close his shutters while the Princess went to the bath.
pages.scene: The marketplace. The herald reads from the scroll â€” everyone must stay at home and close shutters while the Princess goes to and from the bath.

pages.caption: He hid himself behind the door of the bath, and peeped through a chink.
pages.scene: The streets, now empty and shuttered. Aladdin hides behind the door of the bath house, peering through a chink.
pages.action: Aladdin hides behind the door and peeps through a chink.

pages.caption: The Princess lifted her veil as she went in, and looked so beautiful.
pages.scene: The bath house entrance. The Princess lifts her veil as she enters, revealing her face â€” radiant and beautiful.

pages.caption: Aladdin fell in love with her at first sight.
pages.scene: The bath house. Aladdin stares, struck by love at first sight.

pages.caption: He went home so changed that his mother was frightened.
pages.scene: Aladdin's home. He enters, transformed â€” his face gaunt, his eyes distant. His mother startles at the sight of him.
pages.action: Aladdin goes home so changed that his mother is frightened.

pages.caption: He told her he loved the Princess so deeply that he could not live without her.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin sits on a stool, speaking earnestly to his mother.
pages.action: Aladdin tells his mother he loves the Princess.

pages.caption: He meant to ask her in marriage of her father.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin stands, his jaw set with determination.

pages.caption: His mother, on hearing this, burst out laughing.
pages.scene: The home. His mother laughs aloud, covering her mouth in disbelief.

pages.caption: Aladdin at last prevailed upon her to go before the Sultan and carry his request.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin pleads with his mother, his hands clasped. She finally relents.

pages.caption: She fetched a napkin and laid in it the magic fruits from the enchanted garden.
pages.scene: The home. His mother takes a napkin and carefully lays in it the magic fruits from the enchanted garden.
pages.action: She fetches a napkin and lays in it the magic fruits.

pages.caption: Which sparkled and shone like the most beautiful jewels.
pages.scene: The home. The fruits sparkle and shine on the napkin, radiant as jewels.

pages.caption: She took these with her to please the Sultan, and set out, trusting in the lamp.
pages.scene: The palace entrance. Aladdin's mother carries the napkin of treasures, walking with purpose.
pages.action: She took these with her to please the Sultan, trusting in the lamp.

pages.caption: The Grand Vizier and the lords of council had just gone in as she entered the hall.
pages.characters: The Sultan, the Grand Vizier, lords of council
pages.scene: The Sultan's audience chamber. The Grand Vizier and lords of council are assembled before the throne.

pages.caption: She placed herself in front of the Sultan. He, however, took no notice of her.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. Aladdin's mother stands in front of the Sultan, holding the napkin. He does not look at her.

pages.caption: She went every day for a week, and stood in the same place.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. Day after day, Aladdin's mother stands in the same place, unnoticed.
pages.action: She went every day for a week, and stood in the same place.

pages.caption: When the council broke up on the sixth day the Sultan said to his Vizier.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The council breaks up on the sixth day. The Sultan turns to his Vizier.

pages.caption: I see a certain woman in the audience-chamber every day carrying something in a napkin.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan gestures toward the woman standing in the hall.

pages.caption: Call her next time, that I may find out what she wants.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan speaks with authority.

pages.caption: Next day, at a sign from the Vizier, she went up to the foot of the throne.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The next day. At a sign from the Vizier, Aladdin's mother walks forward.
pages.action: She went up to the foot of the throne.

pages.caption: She remained kneeling till the Sultan said to her: Rise, good woman, and tell me what you want.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. Aladdin's mother kneels before the Sultan, the napkin of treasures in her hands.

pages.caption: Before I tell you, I must beg your pardon for my boldness.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. Aladdin's mother stands, her head bowed, speaking carefully.

pages.caption: The Sultan assured her he was not angry.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan nods, assuring her he is not angry.

pages.caption: So she told him of her son's violent love for the Princess.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. Aladdin's mother speaks of her son's love for the Princess.

pages.caption: I pray you to grant his request.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. Aladdin's mother kneels again, her hands clasped in supplication.

pages.caption: The Sultan looked at the gift, and was astonished at its beauty.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan looks at the gift the mother has brought, his eyes wide with astonishment.
pages.action: The Sultan looks at the gift and is astonished at its beauty.

pages.caption: He could not think of marrying his daughter to anyone who could not bring him four trays of gold.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan speaks his condition.

pages.caption: From the gardens of the palace.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan gestures toward the palace gardens.

pages.caption: When she told Aladdin what the Sultan had said.
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin's mother tells him what the Sultan said. Aladdin's face lights up.

pages.caption: He at once had recourse to the genie.
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The home. Aladdin rubs the lamp, summoning the genie.
pages.action: Aladdin has recourse to the genie.

pages.caption: Who brought him four trays of gold and precious stones, far richer than the Sultan had demanded.
pages.characters: The Genie of the Lamp, Aladdin
pages.scene: The home. The genie presents four trays of gold and precious stones, far richer than the Sultan demanded.

pages.caption: The Sultan was so overpowered with this magnificent gift.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan stares at the magnificent trays, overwhelmed.

pages.caption: He immediately agreed to the marriage.
pages.scene: The audience chamber. The Sultan nods in agreement, smiling.

pages.caption: The Grand Vizier, who had set his heart on the Princess marrying his son.
pages.scene: A private chamber. The Grand Vizier stands before the Sultan, his face tight with jealousy.

pages.caption: He told the Sultan he could not understand how anyone could bring such a treasure.
pages.scene: The private chamber. The Vizier gestures suspiciously.

pages.caption: The Sultan did not trouble himself about this, and the wedding was fixed for a fortnight after.
pages.scene: The private chamber. The Sultan waves off the Vizier's concerns, unconcerned.

pages.caption: When the day arrived, Aladdin had the genie dress him in magnificent clothes.
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: Aladdin's home. The day of the wedding arrives. Aladdin stands before the genie, dressed in magnificent clothes.
pages.action: The genie dresses Aladdin in magnificent clothes.

pages.caption: He rode on a beautiful horse, while the Sultan's guard went before him, playing upon trumpets.
pages.scene: The city streets. Aladdin rides a beautiful horse through the crowd. The Sultan's guard plays trumpets before him.
pages.action: Aladdin rides on a beautiful horse while trumpets sound.

pages.caption: The people flocked from all sides to see his splendid train.
pages.scene: The city streets. The people flock from all sides to watch the procession, craning their necks.

pages.caption: Everyone admired his generosity and fine appearance.
pages.scene: The city streets. The townspeople murmur in admiration.

pages.caption: When he reached the palace, the Princess was delighted with his handsome looks.
pages.scene: The palace gates. Aladdin arrives, dismounts, and approaches the entrance. The Princess watches from a window, delighted.

pages.caption: And the Sultan with his generosity.
pages.scene: The palace gates. The Sultan watches from above, pleased.

pages.caption: But the Grand Vizier's son was overcome with envy.
pages.scene: A private chamber in the palace. The Grand Vizier's son watches through a window, his fists clenched.

pages.caption: Aladdin went up to the throne, and laid the trays of gold and precious stones before the Sultan.
pages.scene: The throne room. Aladdin ascends to the throne and lays the trays of gold and precious stones before the Sultan.
pages.action: Aladdin lays the trays before the Sultan.

pages.caption: Then he led the Princess to the bath.
pages.scene: The palace. Aladdin takes the Princess by the hand and leads her to the bath.
pages.action: Aladdin leads the Princess to the bath.

pages.caption: He presented her with the richest of robes.
pages.scene: The bath house. Aladdin presents the Princess with the richest of robes.

pages.caption: And to her attendants he gave such splendid dresses as made them appear like queens.
pages.scene: The bath house. Aladdin presents the attendants with splendid dresses.
pages.action: He gives the attendants splendid dresses.

pages.caption: Aladdin took the Princess by the hand and led her to the throne.
pages.scene: The throne room. Aladdin takes the Princess by the hand and leads her to the throne.
pages.action: Aladdin leads the Princess to the throne.

pages.caption: The Sultan received them with delight, and ordered that the marriage should take place without delay.
pages.scene: The throne room. The Sultan receives them with delight, raising his hand in blessing.

pages.caption: In the meantime, the African magician had returned to his own country, full of rage.
pages.scene: A distant land. The African magician returns to his own country, his face twisted with rage.

pages.caption: He was determined to get the lamp out of Aladdin's possession.
pages.scene: The magician's study. Magic books and scrolls surround him. He paces, plotting.

pages.caption: He took a quantity of new lamps, and went to the palace, crying: New lamps for old!
pages.scene: The city streets near the palace. The magician carries a bundle of new lamps, crying out to passersby.
pages.action: The magician goes to the palace crying: New lamps for old!

pages.caption: The Princess, hearing the noise, sent to see what he was offering.
pages.scene: The palace. The Princess hears the noise from the window and sends a servant to investigate.

pages.caption: He told her he was giving new lamps for old ones.
pages.scene: The palace gates. The servant speaks to the magician, who shows his new lamps.
pages.action: The magician tells the servant he is giving new lamps for old ones.

pages.caption: The Princess, thinking it was a good bargain, sent for Aladdin's old lamp.
pages.scene: The palace. The Princess, thinking it a good bargain, orders Aladdin's old lamp to be given to the magician.
pages.action: She sent for Aladdin's old lamp.

pages.caption: A servant snatched it from her and carried it away.
pages.scene: The palace. A servant snatches the lamp from the Princess's hand before it reaches the magician.
pages.action: The servant snatches the lamp and carries it away.

pages.caption: The servant then went to the magician and got a new lamp in exchange.
pages.scene: The palace gates. The servant gives the old lamp to the magician and receives a new one in exchange.
pages.action: The servant goes to the magician and gets a new lamp in exchange.

pages.caption: When the magician had the lamp in his possession, he at once rubbed it.
pages.scene: A private spot. The magician holds the old lamp, his eyes gleaming. He rubs it.

pages.caption: And the genie appeared.
pages.characters: The African Magician, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The genie appears before the magician, towering and fearsome.

pages.caption: Take me and the Princess, he commanded, and set us down in some far-off country.
pages.scene: The magician commands the genie, his voice commanding.

pages.caption: In a moment they were transported to Africa.
pages.scene: In an instant, the palace and the Princess vanish. The Sultan's palace stands empty.

pages.caption: The magician shut the Princess up in his palace, and then returned to his own house.
pages.scene: A castle in Africa. The magician shuts the Princess up in a room, then leaves.
pages.action: The magician shut the Princess up in his palace.

pages.caption: When the Sultan heard of the disappearance of his daughter and son-in-law, he was beside himself with grief.
pages.scene: The Sultan's throne room. The Sultan learns of his daughter's disappearance. He is beside himself with grief.

pages.caption: Aladdin, who had been out hunting, returned to find the palace empty.
pages.scene: The palace grounds. Aladdin returns from hunting to find the palace empty. He stares in disbelief.

pages.caption: He was so distressed that he wept bitterly.
pages.scene: The palace grounds. Aladdin falls to his knees, weeping bitterly.
pages.action: He was so distressed that he wept bitterly.

pages.caption: The Sultan's guards seized him and dragged him before the throne.
pages.scene: The throne room. The Sultan's guards seize Aladdin and drag him before the throne.
pages.action: The guards seized Aladdin and dragged him before the throne.

pages.caption: The Sultan was so angry that he would have had Aladdin killed.
pages.scene: The throne room. The Sultan glares down at Aladdin, his face contorted with anger.

pages.caption: But the people pleaded for him, for they loved him.
pages.scene: The throne room. The people cry out from the gallery, pleading for Aladdin's life.

pages.caption: At last the Sultan consented to spare his life, on condition that he would bring back the Princess within forty days.
pages.scene: The throne room. The Sultan relents, his hand raised in concession.

pages.caption: Aladdin agreed to this, and set out on his journey.
pages.scene: The throne room. Aladdin agrees and sets out on his journey.
pages.action: Aladdin agreed to this, and set out on his journey.

pages.caption: He travelled for many days, and at last came to the foot of a high mountain.
pages.scene: A high mountain. Aladdin travels for many days and comes to a small cottage. An old woman sits inside spinning.
pages.action: He asks her if she knows where the Princess is.

pages.caption: She told him that she had heard she was in a castle in Africa, built by the magician.
pages.scene: The cottage. The old woman tells Aladdin she has heard the Princess is in a castle in Africa, built by the magician.

pages.caption: Aladdin begged her to help him, and she gave him a magic ring.
pages.scene: The cottage. The old woman gives Aladdin a magic ring for protection.
pages.action: She gave him a magic ring which would protect him from all harm.

pages.caption: He put it on his finger, and at once found himself in the palace where the Princess was.
pages.scene: The castle in Africa. Aladdin puts on the ring and finds himself instantly inside the Princess's room.
pages.action: He put it on his finger, and at once found himself in the palace where the Princess was.

pages.caption: He found her sitting in a room, weeping bitterly.
pages.scene: A room in the castle. The Princess sits alone, weeping bitterly. Her face is streaked with tears.

pages.caption: When she saw him, she was overjoyed, and they embraced each other tenderly.
pages.scene: The room. The Princess sees Aladdin and leaps to her feet, her face lighting with joy.
pages.action: She was overjoyed, and they embraced each other tenderly.

pages.caption: Aladdin told her he would kill the magician and set her free.
pages.scene: The room. Aladdin speaks to the Princess, his face set with determination.

pages.caption: She told him that the magician kept the wonderful lamp in a box in his room.
pages.scene: The room. The Princess tells Aladdin where the lamp is kept.

pages.caption: Aladdin went to the magician's room and found the box.
pages.scene: The magician's room. Aladdin enters and finds a box. He opens it and takes out the lamp.
pages.action: Aladdin went to the magician's room and found the box.

pages.caption: He opened it, took out the lamp, and rubbed it.
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The magician's room. Aladdin opens the box, takes out the lamp, and rubs it.
pages.action: He opened it, took out the lamp, and rubbed it.

pages.caption: The genie appeared and asked what he would have.
pages.characters: Aladdin, the Genie of the Lamp
pages.scene: The magician's room. The genie appears before Aladdin.

pages.caption: Aladdin commanded him to take the magician and set him down in the middle of the desert.
pages.scene: The magician's room. Aladdin commands the genie to take the magician away.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The desert. The magician is transported to the barren wastes, alone and helpless.

pages.caption: Then he commanded him to take the palace and all it contained, and transport it back.
pages.scene: The castle. Aladdin commands the genie to transport the palace and all it contains back to its former place.

pages.caption: In a moment it was done, and the Sultan saw the palace in its old place, and was overjoyed.
pages.scene: The Sultan's palace grounds. The palace reappears in its old place. The Sultan sees it and is overjoyed.

pages.caption: The magician was never seen again.
pages.scene: The palace. The magician is never seen again.

pages.caption: And Aladdin and the Princess lived happily together for many years.
pages.scene: The palace. Aladdin and the Princess stand together, happy and at peace, surrounded by beauty and prosperity.
